html:
A tropical cyclone that struck Mozambique, Malawi and Zimbabwe in March 2019 and left more than 1,500 people dead. It is the deadliest cyclone on record in the southwest Indian Ocean.

It formed as a depression off Mozambique on 4 March and dropped heavy rain on Mozambique and Malawi while it crossed land. Back over the Mozambique Channel it quickly grew into an intense cyclone, then made landfall near the port city of Beira on the night of 14 to 15 March.

The winds wrecked much of Beira, but the rain did worse. Rivers burst their banks and turned the low plains inland into a shallow sea, leaving people on rooftops and in trees for days. In eastern Zimbabwe, floods and landslides buried homes in the Chimanimani district. About three million people were affected, and cholera broke out in the flooded areas. Like the floods of 2000, Idai showed how exposed the low coast is, and it is often cited in talk of climate change.
sum: A tropical cyclone that struck Mozambique, Malawi and Zimbabwe in March 2019 and left more than 1,500 people dead. It is the deadliest cyclone on record in the southwest Indian Ocean.
